clue.text: Porridge maybe? Visit company stocking it

indicators.note: the two words visit company hold the solution in their letters, as a stocking holds what is put in it

explanation.surface: A puzzled host asks whether a visiting firm brought porridge oats in with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge here is not oatmeal but the BBC comedy set in a prison, starring Ronnie Barker; the question mark warns it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge was a celebrated British situation comedy, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Benefit from merger, say, releasing a bit of work in city

indicators.note: the word say lets go of the letter a

parts.note: the word as written, before losing a letter

indicators.note: the work unit goes inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Talk of a merger's benefits, with a piece of work left in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link meaning 'for example' but is wordplay: SAY minus A gives SY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the extra gain from combining, when the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.

clue.text: Rather upset, having swallowed one bone

indicators.note: the reversed letters take the other piece inside them
in a down clue, upset turns the phrase upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a bit means rather, as in a bit tired
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone rather distressed after swallowing a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses A BIT to TIBA, which then swallows I.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone is the larger of the two lower leg bones.

clue.text: Like ring road section during test

indicators.note: the section word is placed within the test word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a bit is a section or part

explanation.surface: A driving test that includes a stretch of the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: London's M25 ring motorway is known as the London Orbital.
explanation.definitionFit: A road circling a city is described this way, encircling it like a satellite's path.

clue.text: Extremely happy taking part in best classes

definitions.note: a phylum is the rank grouping several biological classes, so the plural clue word names what the singular unit is made of

indicators.note: the pick goes into the middle of the other piece, becoming part of it

parts.note: a plum job or role is the best one

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word happy are used

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be placed in the top sets at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classes' looks like school groups but is biological taxonomy: a phylum sits above class in the ranking.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological taxonomy a phylum is the rank that groups related classes together.

clue.text: Defeat current racket appearing in The Mercury

indicators.note: the current and racket pieces show up inside the mercury symbol

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
I is the symbol for electric current
din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A sports report: a beaten team's noisy protest printed in the local paper, The Mercury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Mercury' reads as a newspaper title but is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a heavy beating or thrashing, so a crushing loss in sport.

clue.text: Corn grows here — not much to eat at first

parts.note: little means not much

indicators.note: only the opening letter of eat is used

explanation.surface: Where maize grows there is little food to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corn' is not grain but a hard patch of skin on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn is a callus on the foot, and the smallest digit is a common place for one.

clue.text: Mike bore nasty 14

definitions.note: refers to the solution of 14 down, a bug

parts.note: mic is short for microphone, a mike

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned bad, so the letters of bore are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man called Mike is a horrible dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ, the bug of the cross-reference, is a microscopic organism like this.

clue.text: Order huge necktie to keep performing for fun

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the performing word within them
to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put in a new sequence

parts.note: on means performing, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: Buy an outsized tie to wear on stage, for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges HUGE NECKTIE as TGUEINCHEEK, which keeps ON after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something this way means saying it ironically, as a joke rather than seriously.

clue.text: Ignore number in boat

indicators.note: the abbreviation for number goes inside the word for the boat

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a boat

explanation.surface: Someone told to disregard a figure written inside a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to ignore or cold-shoulder them deliberately.

clue.text: Horses stood nervously in group

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the word for a group

parts.note: a block is a group, as in a block of shares or seats

indicators.note: something done nervously is jittery and disordered, so the letters of stood are jumbled

explanation.surface: A herd of horses stands fidgeting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervously' makes ODSTO; the clue reads as horses standing restlessly in a group, hiding that 'group' is the outer word split open around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodstock is the collective term for thoroughbred horses bred for racing.

clue.text: Animal circles farmer's last source of milk

indicators.note: the animal word goes round the other letter, encircling it

parts.note: a beast is an animal

indicators.note: only the final letter of farmer's is taken

explanation.surface: A beast prowls round the farmer's last cow, the one still giving milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammals feed their young from the mammary gland, which is where milk comes from.

clue.text: A bundle of nerves, band meets hero

parts.note: a gang is a band of people
a lion is a celebrated, heroic person, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: A jittery person meets a pop group's star frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bundle of nerves' reads as a nervous person, but it is meant literally: a knot of nerve cells.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy this is a cluster of nerve cell bodies, literally a bundle of nerves.

clue.text: I cried during speech, being stared at

indicators.note: when spoken, the phrase sounds like the entered word

parts.note: I bawled: to bawl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to weeping while giving a speech under everyone's gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard, so this is a synonym for looked at fixedly.

clue.text: Bug etc turns up in contents of meal prior to X-ray

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit inside the element

parts.words: contents of meal prior to X-ray
parts.note: a barium meal is swallowed before an X-ray of the gut

indicators.note: in a down clue the word etc is turned upside down, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A germ and other things show up in the stomach contents before an X-ray.
explanation.walkthrough: A barium meal is a chalky drink swallowed so the gut shows on an X-ray; 'turns up' gives CTE, read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is informally called a bug, and this single-celled organism is that sort of germ.

clue.text: At least one drop should help this fashion lacking length

definitions.text: At least one drop should help this

indicators.note: the letter for length is missing from the word for fashion

parts.note: style is fashion

explanation.surface: Advice that a drop of something will fix a fashion that is too short.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'drop' is an eye-drop, used to soothe an eyelid infection.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflamed swelling on the eyelid is commonly treated with eye-drops.

clue.text: Mark correct disease vector

definitions.meaning: to put a checkmark against something to show it is right
a blood-sucking arachnid that carries Lyme disease

explanation.surface: A teacher grades a biology answer about how diseases spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkmark confirms an answer, and the parasitic arachnid of that name spreads Lyme disease.

clue.text: Name first words of 'Somewhere'

definitions.meaning: a female first name, as of the saint of Avila
the West Side Story song Somewhere opens with two words meaning a place exists

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking for the name in a song's opening line.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, and split in two it begins the Sondheim–Bernstein lyric of Somewhere.

clue.text: Cultivated angelicas offering relief

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so these letters are dug up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Garden-grown angelica plants are said to soothe pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkilling drug relieves pain, so as an adjective it describes something giving relief.

clue.text: Spoil left overs then finish

parts.note: O stands for over or overs in cricket scoring
to use up is to finish something off

explanation.surface: Ruin the leftovers and then eat them all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left overs' looks like leftovers but splits into L and O, the cricket scorecard letter for overs.
explanation.definitionFit: To mess up or botch something is to ruin it, and this slang phrase means the same.

clue.text: Slight cut in hormone

indicators.note: the word for slight is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an insult is a slight

explanation.surface: A minor cut treated with an injected hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective meaning small, but it is the noun meaning an affront.
explanation.definitionFit: This pancreatic hormone regulates blood sugar.

clue.text: Spot empty mousetrap in big house

indicators.note: those letters go inside the house word

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house

indicators.note: the word mousetrap is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone spots an empty mousetrap in a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot on the skin is a small inflamed blemish of this kind.

clue.text: Wild swimmer always dives in

indicators.note: the word for always plunges into the middle of the swimmer word

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A frantic swimmer keeps plunging into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish activity is frenzied and frantic, the same sense as wild.

clue.text: Cocky parish priest is seen in posh hotel

indicators.note: the parish, priest and is pieces appear inside the posh and hotel letters

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
P is the abbreviation for parish

explanation.surface: A self-important local vicar is spotted in an upmarket hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the 'U and non-U' classification of British speech habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppish behaviour is arrogant and self-assertive, much like cocky.

clue.text: Vegan food that's often taken by medical staff

definitions.meaning: an edible seed such as lentils or beans, a staple of plant-based diets

definitions.text: that's often taken by medical staff
definitions.meaning: the heartbeat that nurses measure at the wrist

explanation.surface: A plant-based dish frequently eaten by hospital workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils and beans are legumes eaten by vegans, and nurses routinely take a patient's heart rate.

clue.text: Border is quiet at this place, one of two in the world

definitions.text: one of two in the world

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
here means at this place

explanation.surface: A peaceful frontier spot claimed as one of only two in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe divides into northern and southern halves, so each half is one of a pair.

clue.text: Pacify Liberals mobbing leader of Unionists

indicators.note: a crowd of Liberals surrounds the other letter, as a mob surrounds someone

parts.note: L is Liberal; plural, here three of them

indicators.note: only the first letter of Unionists is taken

explanation.surface: Liberal politicians crowd round the Unionist leader to calm him down.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Ls make the mob of Liberals; the U goes in after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To lull is to soothe or calm someone, a synonym of pacify.

clue.text: Band play, heading off across river

indicators.note: the shortened play lies across the river letter, spanning it
the play title loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A band plays a Shakespeare tragedy, then sets off over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' takes the H from HAMLET, leaving AMLET, which goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a band of metal or cloth worn around the upper arm.

clue.text: Organ spotted outside public library

indicators.note: the spotted word goes around the library letters

parts.note: seen means spotted

explanation.surface: An organ is noticed just outside the town library.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an abdominal organ that filters blood.
